name: Sudan
note: Every fact is paraphrased from the quoted sentence of the linked source, and dated with that source's publication date. Run python scripts/verify_profiles.py to check each quote against its source.

facts.text: War between the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) began in April 2023 and has spread from Khartoum to Darfur, Kordofan and other regions.
facts.quote: The conflict erupted in April 2023 following a power struggle between the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF), plunging the country into a civil war that has spread from the capital Khartoum to Darfur, Kordofan and other regions.

facts.text: El Fasher, the last SAF stronghold in Darfur, fell to the RSF in October 2025 after an 18-month siege.
facts.quote: El Fasher, the last SAF stronghold in Darfur, fell to the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) in October 2025 after an 18-months siege.

facts.text: About 33.7 million people, around two thirds of the population, are expected to need humanitarian assistance in 2026.
facts.quote: An estimated 33.7 million people – around two thirds of the population – are expected to need humanitarian assistance in 2026.

facts.text: In North Kordofan, El Obeid has faced siege-like conditions for months, with both sides increasingly using drones.
facts.quote: In North Kordofan, El Obeid faced siege-like conditions for months, amid increasing use of drones by both parties.

facts.text: In mid-October 2026, at least 12 children were reportedly killed in two attacks in West Kordofan and Khartoum states.
facts.quote: At least 12 children, some as young as two, were reportedly killed in two separate incidents in Sudan's West Kordofan and Khartoum states in recent days.

facts.text: Close to nine million people were displaced inside Sudan at the end of March 2026.
facts.quote: Conflict-driven displacement remains at extremely high levels, with close to nine million people uprooted within Sudan as of the end of March 2026.
facts.source: FAO, WFP and UNICEF (joint release on the IPC analysis)

facts.text: Thousands of women are returning to Khartoum after years of displacement inside Sudan and in neighbouring countries.
facts.quote: Back in Khartoum, thousands of women are also returning after years of displacement across Sudan and in neighbouring countries.

facts.text: In October 2026 the IPC warned of a growing risk of famine in parts of Greater Darfur and Greater Kordofan, driven by conflict, mass displacement, severe drought and too little funding.
facts.quote: The IPC is warning of a growing risk of famine across parts of Greater Darfur and Greater Kordofan, where conflict, mass displacement, severe drought and inadequate humanitarian funding are driving a rapidly deteriorating situation.

facts.text: The latest full IPC analysis found nearly 19.5 million people, two in five, facing crisis levels of acute food insecurity (IPC Phase 3 or above).
facts.quote: nearly 19.5 million people – two out of every five people in Sudan - are currently facing crisis levels of acute food insecurity (IPC Phase 3 or above) across Sudan, according to the latest Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC) analysis.
facts.source: FAO, WFP and UNICEF (joint release on the IPC analysis)

facts.text: An estimated 825,000 children under five are expected to suffer severe acute malnutrition in 2026.
facts.quote: An estimated 825,000 children under five are expected to suffer from Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) in 2026
facts.source: FAO, WFP and UNICEF (joint release on the IPC analysis)

facts.text: By 2026, 37% of Sudan's health facilities had stopped functioning.
facts.quote: By 2026, 37% of the country’s health facilities had stopped functioning.

facts.text: Since April 2023, WHO has verified 228 attacks on health care, causing 2,055 deaths and 817 injuries.
facts.quote: Since 15 April 2023, WHO has verified 228 attacks on health care that have led to 2055 deaths and 817 injuries.

facts.text: An estimated 17 million people lack safe drinking water and 24 million lack adequate sanitation.
facts.quote: an estimated 17 million people lack access to safe drinking water, and 24 million people lack access to adequate sanitation.
facts.source: FAO, WFP and UNICEF (joint release on the IPC analysis)

facts.text: In Darfur, nearly three quarters of schools have been damaged, destroyed or made non-functional since April 2023.
facts.quote: In battle-scarred Darfur alone, nearly three quarters of schools have been damaged, destroyed or otherwise rendered non-functional since fighting erupted in April 2023.

facts.text: Since 2024 the UN has verified more than 67 attacks on schools, and over 154 cases of military use of schools have been reported.
facts.quote: since 2024, the UN has verified more than 67 attacks on schools across Sudan, while over 154 instances of military use of schools have been reported, though the true scale is undoubtedly greater.

facts.text: The 2026 humanitarian response plan has been cut to a “basic survival package” and was only 41% funded by September 2026.
facts.quote: Yet the humanitarian response plan has been cut to a “basic survival package.” By September 2026, the plan was only 41 percent funded.

not_covered: Shelter: no 2026 source with figures was found.
